terms.def: EU status for medicines monitored more closely, shown by an inverted black triangle in the SmPC and leaflet.
The labelling (IIIA) and package leaflet (IIIB) of a centrally authorised product.
The list of national reporting systems for suspected adverse reactions, referred to in SmPC 4.8 and leaflet section 4.
An area on the outer packaging of a centrally authorised product for national particulars such as price.
Showing that a leaflet is similar enough to a user-tested leaflet that a new test is not needed.
Electronic product information: the SmPC and leaflet as structured data (EU standard based on HL7 FHIR).
An excipient listed in the annex to the excipients guideline, needing a set statement in the product information.
Member states’ review of the translations of a centrally authorised product’s product information.
The EU patient information that comes in the pack (Annex IIIB).
Pharmacovigilance Risk Assessment Committee of EMA; recommends safety wording and deadlines.
Periodic safety update single assessment: one EU assessment of PSURs for an active substance.
Quality Review of Documents: the EMA group that publishes the product information templates.
Summary of Product Characteristics: the EU product information for health professionals (Annex I).
The serialised code in a 2D data matrix on EU prescription packs (Delegated Regulation 2016/161).
Testing a leaflet with members of the public; each question passes when 16 of 20 find and understand the answer.
